description: We are Terra Nexis, an independent student-led technology team from Faisalabad, Pakistan. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to combine AI, web development, and NASA Earth observation data to address agricultural challenges through our selected challenge, "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data." Our goal is to turn satellite data into useful insights that support smarter agricultural decisions.
summary:
AgriOrbit AI is an AI-powered agricultural intelligence platform designed to help farmers make smarter, data-informed decisions using satellite and environmental data. We developed a web-based platform that connects agricultural insights with location-based field analysis, helping users understand the conditions affecting their farmland.

The platform focuses on making space-based information more accessible and useful for everyday farming. It aims to help users explore their locations, assess selected fields, understand vegetation health through indicators such as NDVI, monitor environmental conditions, and receive AI-assisted agricultural insights and recommendations.

AgriOrbit AI addresses the **Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data** challenge by turning complex Earth-observation information into practical insights that farmers can understand and use. This is important because farmers face changing environmental conditions, water challenges, and uncertainty about crop health. By making satellite-based information easier to interpret, AgriOrbit AI aims to support more informed, sustainable, and climate-aware farming decisions, with a vision to serve agricultural communities worldwide.
details:
AgriOrbit AI — Project Details

AgriOrbit AI is an AI-powered agricultural intelligence platform designed to make satellite and environmental information more accessible and useful for farmers. Its goal is to connect Earth-observation data with understandable, location-based agricultural insights, helping users better understand the conditions affecting their farmland.

What does it do and how does it work?

AgriOrbit AI provides a web-based environment where users can explore agricultural locations and, where supported, focus on a specific field or geographical area. The platform aims to bring together different types of agricultural and environmental information, including vegetation indicators, weather-related information, and other available Earth-observation insights.

One of its important concepts is location-based analysis: instead of presenting only general agricultural information, the platform is designed to help users investigate the area they are interested in. Indicators such as the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) can help users understand vegetation greenness and condition. The platform also includes Smarty AI, an agricultural intelligence assistant intended to explain technical information in simpler language and provide AI-assisted guidance.

What benefits does it offer?

AgriOrbit AI aims to:

  • Make satellite-based agricultural information easier to understand.
  • Help users explore environmental conditions affecting their selected locations.
  • Improve awareness of vegetation health indicators.
  • Support more informed agricultural planning.
  • Make complex geospatial information more accessible to people without specialist technical knowledge.

Intended impact

Our long-term vision is to make Earth-observation information more useful to agricultural communities worldwide. By helping users understand their land and the environmental conditions around it, AgriOrbit AI aims to support informed, sustainable, and climate-aware agricultural decisions.

Tools and development

AgriOrbit AI was developed as a web-based technology project using AI-assisted development tools. The development process involved designing the user experience, planning the platform's features, building its interface, and developing its agricultural intelligence concept.

The project combines web technologies, geospatial information concepts, satellite-data resources, and AI-assisted interaction. The exact programming languages, libraries, APIs, and hosting services used should be identified from the final implementation.

Creativity and innovation

The creative aspect of AgriOrbit AI is its attempt to bring space-based observations, geographical exploration, and AI-assisted agricultural explanations together in one accessible platform. Rather than expecting farmers to interpret complex scientific datasets independently, the project aims to present relevant information in a clearer and more practical way.

Factors considered

During development, we considered accessibility, ease of use, global agricultural relevance, geographical accuracy, scientific reliability, and the limitations of satellite-derived information. We also considered the importance of explaining indicators correctly: for example, NDVI is an indicator of vegetation conditions, not a direct diagnosis of crop disease or a guarantee of crop yield.

AgriOrbit AI is designed with the vision of making agricultural intelligence more understandable and accessible, helping connect information gathered from space with decisions made on the ground.
